clue.text: Out of harmony with a return of British rule

indicators.note: a return turns the word for British rule so it reads backwards

parts.note: the Raj was British rule in India

explanation.surface: Someone has fallen out with a revival of colonial government in India.
explanation.walkthrough: The Raj was British rule in India; 'Out of harmony' sounds musical but means slightly open, as of a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A door ajar is not closed; figuratively, jarring or discordant, at odds with something.

clue.text: After revision, perform some man's work

indicators.note: revision means the letters of the word after are revised into a new order

parts.note: to act is to perform on stage

explanation.surface: Once edited, a man's labour is staged.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'After' a time word; it is the fodder for 'revision'.
explanation.definitionFit: An artefact is an object made by human hands, a product of human craft.

clue.text: Revolutionary means to keep gear moving round

definitions.meaning: a political stirrer, one who stirs up unrest

definitions.text: means to keep gear moving round
definitions.meaning: the paddle in a washing machine that churns clothes about

explanation.definitionFit: An agitator stirs up political trouble; it is also the churning device inside a washing machine.

clue.text: It says one can go on common land

definitions.text: It says one can go on common land

parts.words: It says one can go on common land
parts.note: a signal of permission to proceed, with a pun on the village green as common land

explanation.surface: A notice says the public may walk across the common.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sign permitting access; the pun is that common land is a 'green', and the go-ahead signal is a coloured lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A permission signal like the go colour on traffic signals, meaning one may proceed.

clue.text: Sport with doctor at a dance

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union, a sport
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A sportsman and a medic are at a dance together.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance in a lively rhythm.

clue.text: Underground traveller's terribly hot, getting warmer

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition reads as the creature itself

indicators.note: terribly means the letters are jumbled badly into a new order

explanation.surface: A Tube passenger is dreadfully hot, getting hotter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges HOT and WARMER together. 'Underground traveller' suggests a Tube passenger in London.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthworm burrows through soil, so it moves about below ground.

clue.text: Disagreeable firm that employs hacks

parts.note: livery means irritable or bilious, as with a bad liver
something firm is stable, steady

explanation.surface: A nasty company hires low-grade journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacks' suggests jobbing journalists; here they are hired horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A livery stable keeps horses for hire, and hired riding horses are called hacks.

clue.text: Talkative chap that helps to move a gondola

definitions.text: that helps to move a gondola
definitions.meaning: the envelope of an airship or balloon, which lifts the gondola slung beneath

explanation.definitionFit: A windbag of a person talks on; the gas envelope of a balloon lifts its cabin or gondola.

clue.text: Area where magpies are ringed

parts.note: in archery and rifle shooting a magpie is a shot striking an outer ring of the board

explanation.surface: Birdwatchers fit leg rings to birds in some patch of land.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests bird-ringing; in shooting, a magpie is a hit in the second ring from the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting board of concentric rings in which a hit in an outer circle is a magpie.

clue.text: See through spray

definitions.meaning: to understand or perceive, informal British sense
a small shoot or sprig from a tree

explanation.definitionFit: Informally one may twig a trick, grasping it; a small leafy shoot is also a spray from a branch.

clue.text: Make-up artist is introduced to old apprentice

indicators.note: one word is introduced into the middle of the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: an improver was an old term for a learner or apprentice
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cosmetics specialist is presented to a former trainee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up artist' suggests cosmetics but means someone who makes things up on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: One who extemporises makes up material as they go along, an artist of the impromptu.

clue.text: Removal of chairperson — then rent demo blows up

indicators.note: blows up suggests an explosion scattering these letters into new order

explanation.surface: A protest erupts after the chair is ousted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blows up' rearranges THEN, RENT and DEMO together; 'chairperson' hides a throne-sitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dethroning removes a monarch from the throne, the seat of state, so the occupant of that chair is removed.

clue.text: Half-covered light put back as illumination for landing

indicators.note: put back tells us the whole assembled run is to be read in reverse
one word is covered by the other, so the light sits inside it

parts.note: a taper is a thin candle, a light

explanation.surface: A partly shaded lamp is replaced to light the way for arriving aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-covered' looks like one adjective but splits into a piece and its indicator; 'put back' then reverses the whole assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: A flarepath is a line of lights or flares marking a runway so aircraft can land at night.

clue.text: Study English author

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it

explanation.surface: A student is reading an English writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, writer of The Cloister and the Hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade was a nineteenth-century English novelist and dramatist, so he is a writer.

clue.text: The short cut into courtyard is drier

indicators.note: one stretch goes into the courtyard word, which surrounds it

parts.note: a close is an enclosed courtyard, as in a cathedral close

indicators.note: cut means the word short loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A quick route through an enclosed yard is less damp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims SHORT to SHOR; THE plus SHOR goes 'into' CLOSE. The surface makes 'drier' an adjective; it is a noun, a thing for drying clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes-horse is a frame on which washing is hung to dry, hence a drier.

clue.text: Penitent was put in this fire by churchmen

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them from a job
the clergy are called the cloth

explanation.surface: A sinner was set on fire by clerics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' looks like flames; it is dismissal. Penitents wore rough garments of this cloth with ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse sackcloth was worn as a sign of mourning or repentance, so a penitent dressed in it.

clue.text: Left point of view voiced in play

indicators.note: voiced means the word for a point of view is spoken, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: an attitude is a standpoint or way of seeing things

explanation.surface: A left-wing opinion is expressed in a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' suggests a drama; it means room for movement. ATTITUDE spoken sounds like ATITUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude is freedom of action or scope, as a rope with some slack has room to move.

clue.text: Boy with pain in side gets needled by surgeon?

parts.note: a stitch is a sharp pain in the side, as when running
Ed is a boy's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A lad with a side ache gets irritated by a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needled' looks like irritated; the question mark flags the sewing sense, a wound closed with needle and thread.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon closes a wound with needle and thread, sewing it shut.

clue.text: Not including corporal, say, and injured batman out of action

indicators.note: one word includes the others inside it, so they go within

parts.note: taken as written, the word not
a corporal is an example of an NCO, a non-commissioned officer

indicators.note: injured signals that the letters of batman are damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: An officer's servant, hurt, is out of the fighting, as is a junior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: A batman is a British officer's personal servant; 'injured' rearranges his letters, and the surface battle picture hides the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-combatant takes no part in fighting, a civilian or medic out of the battle.

clue.text: Soldiers in large numbers in the mess

indicators.note: the soldiers are put in the middle of the word for large numbers

parts.note: a mass is a large quantity or crowd
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Lots of troops are eating together in the canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' suggests the soldiers' dining room but means a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is a bog or a confused muddle, a mess one is stuck in.

clue.text: A knave, perhaps, found among thieves

definitions.meaning: in card games such as whist the jack, ace, king and queen are the high scoring cards
from the proverb that criminals keep faith with one another

explanation.definitionFit: The knave or jack is a court card in bridge scoring; the proverb says thieves keep faith with each other.

clue.text: I put on weight in the invigorating air

indicators.note: put on means the word for I is placed after the weight in this across answer

parts.note: oz is the abbreviation for ounce, a weight
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: Someone gains a few pounds while breathing bracing seaside air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' looks like gaining weight; it signals one piece placed on the other. Bracing seaside air was popularly called ozone.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh bracing sea air was loosely called ozone in Victorian and later British usage.

clue.text: Well-bred heel providing money for royalty

parts.note: civil means courteous, polite, as from good breeding
a ship heels when it leans over, as does one that lists

explanation.surface: A polite cad supplies cash to the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heel' looks like a cad; it is the nautical verb for leaning. The Civil List was the annual grant from Parliament to the British royal household.
explanation.definitionFit: The Civil List was the sum Parliament voted for the upkeep of the sovereign's household.

clue.text: Love of fine art is a good quality, up to a point

indicators.note: up to a point means the word stops short of its full length, losing its last letter

parts.note: a virtue is a good quality of character

explanation.surface: An appreciation of the arts is a fine trait, within limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up to a point' looks like 'somewhat'; it cuts VIRTUE short.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtu is a taste for curios and fine objects of art, connoisseurship.

clue.text: Too honourable for directors, to be frank

parts.note: someone too honourable for a mean act is above it
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: Being honest, the speaker says something is beneath the dignity of the management.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Done openly, without concealment, as an honest dealing that is open and candid.

clue.text: Rich Americans' drink

definitions.meaning: in US slang alcohol, liquor, or the act of drinking it

explanation.definitionFit: Lush means luxuriant and plentiful; Americans also used it for liquor and for a heavy drinker.

clue.text: Remove grate no longer in fashion

parts.note: to grate on a surface is to scratch it
something unfashionable is out

explanation.surface: Someone throws away an old-fashioned fireplace grate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grate' looks like a fireplace grate but is the verb, to scrape.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete a word from a page by striking lines through it removes it.

clue.text: Expected female to return hostility

indicators.note: to return means the pieces together are read from the end backwards

parts.note: something due is expected, as a train due at noon

explanation.surface: A woman due back was met with animosity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns both pieces as one unit, so the female's letter ends up first.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running bitter quarrel between families or factions is enmity.
